How x (twitter) fonts works

X posts have no bold or italic button for most accounts, but they accept Unicode letters. Copy a style here and paste it into your post or profile.

Where it helps

Bold a single phrase for emphasis or a thread heading. Keep hashtags and @mentions plain so they still link.

Fonts for X: what works and where

  • Display name: up to 50 characters.
  • Bio: up to 160 characters.
  • Handle: letters, numbers and underscores only.
  • Posts: X counts many Unicode characters, including styled letters and emoji, as two characters toward the limit.

Tips

Styled hashtags do not work as hashtags, and styled words are harder to find in search. Bold one key phrase rather than a whole post.

Limits are as published by X at the time of writing and can change; the app’s own counter is final.

Does fancy text hurt my reach on X?

Styled words are not matched by search, and screen readers may spell them letter by letter. Use them for emphasis, not for the words you want people to find.

Can screen readers read fancy text?

Not reliably. Many screen readers announce each styled letter by its Unicode name or skip it, so a styled phrase can become hard to follow. Style a short accent, and keep important words, links and instructions in ordinary letters.
